study.question: Does explicit intensity of encoded target-field matches separated by action improve normalized attention beyond generic history counts/recency? Supplied static/pooled/DIN AUCs are 0.6050036145/0.6102261137/0.6133619861 on 3234051 validation impressions; Logloss 0.1972554941/0.1970864634/0.1967946465. Source inspection shows category+brand+action+recency added before a softmax weighted mean, with no explicit action-specific field-match counts. This is an observed representational limitation, not evidence of its error contribution. DIN category-match-present AUC0.6107123 versus absent0.6176437 compares different populations and is only descriptive. All three supplied trajectories succeeded; no failed or abandoned research branches were supplied. Raw data, causal audits and training runtime are not exposed in this phase; no independent data-readiness claim is made.
study.hypothesis: A residual predictor of field-preserving, behavior-marked count and recency mass exposes useful target-specific intensity obscured by field addition and normalized averaging. At fixed static features, repeating identical history tuples leaves the reference weighted mean unchanged but changes count mass: an algebraic non-injectivity counterexample, not evidence of prevalence. Both target routing and action labels should contribute beyond generic intensity.

nearest_work.difference: DIN section4.3 already motivates interest intensity. We retain the supplied softmax backbone and test explicit field/action counts; no priority claim.
Read public model.py attention(): author code uses softmax, unlike the paper intensity discussion. The local reference is adapted, not an exact reproduction.

Pinned README confirms category, brand and action but no item identity. We use supplied fields/age only. Publisher full text returned Access Denied; full DMR paper verification and reproduction are not claimed.

inherited_components: Entire baseline embedding lookup, additive history, log2-age embeddings, target-aware attention and classifier
Shared static/history category and brand tables and fixed host training recipe
Existing interest-intensity motivation and standard event aggregation; scientific novelty remains unverified
study.proposed_difference: Add a separate 48->32->1 ReLU residual logit head after constructing the complete baseline. Exactly1601 added parameters; expected total17131876 from baseline17130275. Cube axes: four disjoint encoded-match routes (neither/category-only/brand-only/both), four actions, three fixed kernels (1, exp(-age/86400), exp(-age/604800)). Mask supplied events, exclude zero target IDs from matches, sum within supplied history, apply log1p/ln129. Empty history has zero features, though the learned head bias can contribute a constant. Zero-initialized final head starts at baseline logits. Controls marginalize either or both axes, broadcast evenly before log transform. This is a mechanism-distinct local intervention, not a verified new scientific contribution. Optimizer, loss, data, split, scorer and sample coverage remain fixed.
predictions: Full improves full-population validation AUC over baseline and BOTH single-axis removals; Logloss and costs are separate outcomes. Aggregate gain alone cannot establish the mechanism.
Positive conditional axis effects across paired seeds support useful information; a repeated positive factorial interaction supports joint utility beyond additive effects.

Gains should appear in sufficiently populated existing match/action slices; empty-history gains cannot support matching. Slice localization is exploratory and requires sample/positive/negative counts.
Equal allocated parameters and count computation among variants; cost overhead must be measured by host, not assumed.
falsifiers: Full fails to outperform both_blind or either single-axis removal across paired seeds: no controlled support for the joint claim.
Both_blind reproduces all gain: prefer generic intensity/recency or added-head explanation.
Only the fixed512-example diagnostics prefix or one seed improves: insufficient evidence.
Nonfinite/malformed outputs or timeout are implementation/resource failure, not scientific refutation.
Improved AUC with worse Logloss, latency or rare slices is a tradeoff, not unconditional improvement.
alternative_explanations: Marginalization lowers effective input rank despite equal allocated parameters: an information-removal contrast, not proof against every capacity/regularization explanation.
Count-axis collapse changes feature distributions and optimization geometry after log1p.
Joint training changes backbone representations; this estimates the complete intervention, not causal mediation.
Equality of encoded IDs may reflect hash collisions or shared unknown IDs. Zero is excluded; no other missing/unknown mapping is documented in the API.
Only supplied capped history is counted; saturation at128 and lost rare older actions limit intensity interpretation.
Extra head capacity or easier optimization can explain baseline-relative gain. Equal nominal parameter count does not imply equal effective statistical capacity.
Behavior counts can proxy activity, propensity, user frequency and time; no causal effect of action type is claimed.
Publisher snapshot as-of dates are undocumented under the frozen benchmark assumption; production point-in-time validity is unverified.
